name: Explorium AgentSource
summary: B2B business data for 80M+ companies: match companies to ids, filter and count companies by firmographics, and enrich them with firmographics, technographics, funding, financials, workforce trends, hierarchies and recent business events.

api_key.description: An Explorium AgentSource API key (admin.explorium.ai). Sent in the api_key header.

notes: Calls spend credits by action (the price list is on the admin pricing page); check the balance with explorium.credits.get.
Rate limit: 200 queries a minute per key, where each entity in a batch counts as one query (50 ids = 50 queries). 429 carries Retry-After.
Most calls take Explorium business ids: get them from explorium.businesses.match first, or pass businesses_to_match to an enrichment.
This entry uses the v2 API. Async jobs, dataset uploads, event enrollments, webhooks, prospects and AI research are not in it.

endpoints.name: Match companies to ids
endpoints.summary: Explorium business ids for companies given by name, domain, website URL or LinkedIn URL, in input order.

businesses_to_match.description: Companies to match, each {name, domain, url, linkedin_url}; name plus domain is most reliable.

notes: A read sent as POST with a JSON body: it looks data up and changes nothing.
With name and domain, an unsure match falls back to the domain alone; a name alone relies on fuzzy matching.

endpoints.name: Search companies by filters
endpoints.summary: Companies matching filters such as country, region, size, revenue, age, industry category, tech stack, intent topics or website keywords.

mode.description: Detail level: full. preview (names and domains only) needs a custom plan.

filters.description: Filters object: each field takes {"values": [...]} (OR within a field, AND across fields). Fields include country_code, region_country_code, company_size, company_revenue, company_age, linkedin_category, naics_category, google_category, company_tech_stack_tech, business_intent_topics, website_keywords, is_public_company, has_website; valid values come from explorium.autocomplete.

page.description: Page number from 1; omit for cursor paging.

notes: A read sent as POST with a JSON body: it looks data up and changes nothing.
Only one category filter per request: Google category, LinkedIn industry or NAICS.

endpoints.name: Count companies by filters
endpoints.summary: How many companies match a filter set, broken down by category and location.

filters.description: The same filters object as explorium.businesses.search.

notes: A read sent as POST with a JSON body: it looks data up and changes nothing.

endpoints.name: Autocomplete filter values
endpoints.summary: Valid filter values for a field (countries, regions, categories, tech, sizes, revenue bands, intent topics) from partial text.

field.description: The field to suggest values for.

semantic_search.description: true for broader topic-aware suggestions; meant for business_intent_topics.

businesses_to_match.description: Instead of ids: up to 50 companies as {name, domain, url, linkedin_url}, matched and enriched in one call; unmatched rows come back null and are not charged.

notes: A read sent as POST with a JSON body: it looks data up and changes nothing.

endpoints.name: Get recent business events
endpoints.summary: Recent events for up to 40 companies: funding rounds, IPOs, product launches, offices, partnerships, hires, departmental growth, lawsuits, breaches, cost cutting, M&A.

event_types.description: Event types to return, e.g. new_funding_round, ipo_announcement, new_product, new_office, new_partnership, executive_joined_company, merger_and_acquisitions, lawsuits_and_legal_issues, outages_and_security_breaches, cost_cutting, hiring_in_engineering_department.

timestamp_from.description: Earliest event time, ISO date-time or YYYY-MM-DD; keep it within the last three months.

notes: A read sent as POST with a JSON body: it looks data up and changes nothing.
Recent events only (about the last quarter); for history use the enrichments. An empty answer means nothing happened in the window.
